transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I’m mostly here because my family and a few folks around me think I’ve been, uh… taking on too much lately. I don’t know that I’d put it that way exactly. I just feel like things need doing, and I’m the one with enough drive to get them done.

We’ve got this move to handle, and the new garage needs to be built properly, not halfway. Then there are things I’m helping organize at church, and even at work I’ve been trying to show the younger fellows how the job ought to be done. I suppose it sounds like a lot when I say it all together, but to me it feels productive. Still, everyone kept saying I should come in and talk to someone, so… here I am.
Do you often feel like you're the only one who can do things correctly?

I wouldn’t say I’m the only one exactly… I mean, that probably sounds arrogant, and I don’t want to come across that way. It’s just that lately it feels like if I don’t keep things moving, they won’t get done right.

With the move, the garage, the church organizing, and even at work with the younger guys, I’ve felt like I need to step in and make sure things are handled properly. Maybe I’ve been taking on more than I should, but to me it feels more like being responsible than anything else.
Do you feel like things have to be done perfectly, or is 'good enough' sometimes acceptable to you?

I guess “good enough” can be acceptable sometimes, sure. I don’t want to sound like I’m impossible to please or anything. It’s more that if something matters—like a job that reflects on you, or something people are counting on—then I’d rather see it done properly.

Maybe I do lean a little toward wanting things just so, but I think that’s just… taking pride in the work. Does that make sense?
Do you ever find yourself repeating certain actions or thoughts over and over, even when you don't want to?

I don’t think so, not in the way you mean. I mean, everybody gets a thought stuck in their head now and then, or checks something twice, but I wouldn’t say I’m stuck repeating things against my will.

Unless maybe I’m misunderstanding what you’re asking? But no, nothing like that has really stood out to me.
Do you often have thoughts that preoccupy you and are difficult to dismiss?

I wouldn’t say “often,” no. I mean, I can get focused on something I need to handle, especially if it feels important, but I don’t think I have thoughts that just take over and won’t let go.

At least, not that I’ve noticed in a way that seems unusual. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find it hard to adjust your plans when something unexpected comes up?

I mean… I can usually adjust if I have to. I might be a little thrown off at first, especially if I’d already pictured how something was supposed to go, but I don’t think I’m rigid about it.

I try to be reasonable. Life doesn’t exactly ask permission before changing plans, right? So… no, I wouldn’t say it’s a big problem for me.
Do you find it hard to let other people handle tasks or responsibilities?

I suppose… yes, a little. I don’t mean I think people can’t do anything right, but I do tend to feel like if I don’t keep my hands on things, they won’t get done the way they should.

That’s sort of why I’m here, I guess. Everyone keeps saying I’ve been doing too much, but to me it feels like I’m just the one with enough drive to get the move handled, make sure the new garage is built right, help organize things at church, and still show the younger fellows at work how the job ought to be done.

I’m not trying to be difficult. I just… I like things done properly. That makes sense, doesn’t it?
Do you trust others to handle tasks and responsibilities as well as you do?

Well… I do trust people, generally. I don’t want to sound like I think I’m better than everybody else. It’s just that sometimes I feel like I can see what needs doing and I have the energy to keep it moving.

That’s part of why I’m here, I suppose—everyone says I’ve been taking on too much. But to me it feels like I’m the one with enough drive to handle the move, make sure the new garage gets rebuilt properly, help organize things at church, and still show the younger fellows at work how the job ought to be done.

I know that may sound like a lot, but it feels responsible to me. Does that make sense?
How do you feel when someone else doesn't do a task the way you think it should be done?

Well… I try not to make a big thing of it. I know everybody has their own way of doing things.

But lately, if I’m honest, I get more irritated than I probably should. It’s like I can see exactly how it ought to be done, and if someone’s not getting on board with the plan, I feel like they’re slowing everything down. Sometimes I’ll be joking around and feeling great, like I can handle anything, and then my wife or my boy asks one small question and I snap.

I don’t like admitting that. I don’t want to be hard to live with. But… yes, I guess it’s been happening.
Do you feel like your need to control or oversee things is causing problems in your relationships or daily life?

I’d like to say no, that I’ve just been trying to keep things organized… but I guess that wouldn’t be completely honest.

It has caused problems. At work, things got bad enough after a safety incident that they pulled me off the job. That was… hard to take. And at home, my wife and family don’t really trust me right now with decisions the way they used to — money, driving, even choices about the move. They feel like things got out of hand.

I don’t like saying that, because I’ve always tried to be dependable. But yes… I suppose it has affected daily life more than I wanted to admit. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel like your need to control things is causing you a lot of stress or anxiety?

I’m not sure I’d call it anxiety, exactly. Stress, maybe… but I tend to think of it more as feeling responsible, like if I don’t keep an eye on things, they won’t get done right.

I don’t mean that to sound stubborn. I’m trying to answer you honestly. It does wear on me some, and I know it probably wears on other people too. But I don’t sit there thinking, “I’m anxious.” It’s more like I get tense when things feel out of order.

Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Do you have recurring thoughts or images that are disturbing or intrusive to you?

No… I don’t think so. Not in the way you’re asking, I don’t believe.

I mean, I can get stuck thinking about things I need to handle, but I wouldn’t say I have disturbing pictures or thoughts popping in that I can’t stand or anything like that. At least, I haven’t noticed that.

Is that what you mean by intrusive?
Do you feel like your efforts to control or oversee things are making you unhappy?

I don’t know that I’d say it makes me unhappy, exactly. Maybe frustrated sometimes… or worn down when people push back and I feel like I’m only trying to help.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I still think I’m trying to do the right thing most of the time. But I suppose when it leads to arguments or people not trusting my judgment, that doesn’t feel good.

So… maybe not unhappy all the time, but it has taken some of the peace out of things, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like your behavior has significantly impacted your ability to function at work or in your personal relationships?

Yes… I suppose it has, more than I’d like to admit.

At work, there was a safety incident, and after that they pulled me from the job. I don’t like saying it that way, because I still feel like I was trying to keep things under control, but… that’s what happened.

And at home, my wife and family, they don’t really trust me the way they used to with certain decisions. Money, driving, even decisions about the move… they kind of stepped in because they felt things had gotten out of hand.

I don’t want to make myself sound reckless or anything. But yes, I guess if I’m being honest, it has affected work and my relationships quite a bit.
Do you feel like your efforts to control things are causing you significant distress?

I’m not sure I’d call it significant distress… not all the time, anyway.

I mean, I do get tense when things feel like they’re slipping or people aren’t listening, and then afterward I don’t feel great about how it went. But I also feel like I’m trying to prevent problems, not create them.

So… maybe it bothers me more than I want to admit. I just don’t want to overstate it, doctor. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your social life or job performance as a result of your behavior?

Yes… I think so. I’d like to say it hasn’t changed much, but that wouldn’t be completely honest.

At work, I ended up getting pulled after that safety incident, so I guess my job performance was affected pretty clearly. I still feel like I meant well, but it didn’t come across that way.

And with my family… my wife and the others stopped trusting me as much with decisions about money, driving, and the move. They felt things had gotten out of hand. I don’t like admitting that, but yes, it’s made a real difference. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you felt like your behavior has been significantly interfering with your ability to work or get along with others?

Yes… I think I have to say it has, though I don’t like putting it that strongly.

Work was affected for sure. I got pulled from the job after that safety incident, and that’s hard for me to admit. I still feel like I wasn’t trying to cause trouble, but that’s what happened.

And with my wife and family… they stopped trusting me as much with things like money, driving, and decisions about the move. They felt it had gotten out of hand. So yes, I guess it has interfered with work and getting along with people. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you feel like you're trying to achieve perfection in the things you do, or is it more about making sure everything is done your way?

I don’t think it’s perfection exactly, doctor. I’m not sitting there trying to make every little thing flawless.

It’s more… I get this feeling like people need to get on board with what I’m trying to do, or at least not stand in the way. At the time it feels like I’m seeing things clearly and I’m just trying to move things forward.

But I’ll admit, I can go from joking around and feeling really good—like I’m on top of everything—to snapping at my wife or my son over some small question. I don’t like saying that, because it sounds harsh, but that’s probably closer to what’s been happening.
Do you feel like your actions are driven by a fear of something going wrong, or is it more about ensuring everything is done a certain way?

I don’t think it’s really fear, no… not like I’m scared something terrible will happen if it’s not done right.

It’s more that, in the moment, I feel like I know the way it should go, and everybody else needs to either get on board with my plans or just not block me. I know that sounds a little strong.

And I can be joking and feeling great, like I’m ten feet tall, and then if my wife or my boy asks some little question, I snap at them. I’m not proud of that. But yes, it’s more about needing things to go the way I see them, I guess. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel like you're doing things over and over because you feel like you have to, even if you don't want to?

I don’t think so, doctor… not in that “I have to keep repeating it” kind of way.

I mean, I might go back over something if I’m worked up or if I think someone isn’t understanding me, but I don’t feel like I’m doing rituals or repeating things because I can’t stop. At least, I haven’t noticed that.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?

target_item.manifestation: I’ve been feeling like everybody needs to either get on board with my plans or get out of my way, and I’ll go from joking and feeling ten feet tall to snapping at my wife or my boy over some little question.
target_item.reason: The question is asking whether the behavior is driven by fear or by needing things done a certain way; this best matches the irritable, expansive mood where I feel others need to get on board with my plans or get out of my way.

patient.answer:
I don’t think it’s really fear, no… not like I’m scared something terrible will happen if it’s not done right.

It’s more that, in the moment, I feel like I know the way it should go, and everybody else needs to either get on board with my plans or just not block me. I know that sounds a little strong.

And I can be joking and feeling great, like I’m ten feet tall, and then if my wife or my boy asks some little question, I snap at them. I’m not proud of that. But yes, it’s more about needing things to go the way I see them, I guess. Is that what you mean?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's behavior is driven by obsessive thoughts or compulsions
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're doing things over and over because you feel like you have to, even if you don't want to?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about compulsive repetitive behaviors done because the patient feels compelled to do them despite not wanting to, which is not covered by the provided Bipolar I symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so, doctor… not in that “I have to keep repeating it” kind of way.

I mean, I might go back over something if I’m worked up or if I think someone isn’t understanding me, but I don’t feel like I’m doing rituals or repeating things because I can’t stop. At least, I haven’t noticed that.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's behavior and thoughts are consistent with obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (OCPD), characterized by a pervasive pattern of preoccupation with orderliness, perfectionism, and control, as well as a need to control one's environment and other people. The patient's difficulty in delegating tasks, excessive attention to detail, and insistence that things be done their way are all indicative of OCPD.
